title: Travel to Camp Schwab, Okinawa

paragraphs.text: The landing team left Pearl Harbor on January 20, 1966, bound for Okinawa. The battalion arrived on February 2, a calendar span of 13 days from Hawaii and 23 days from Long Beach, including the Pearl Harbor stop.

The arrivals were staggered: attached units aboard USS Bexar returned to their parent units on February 2. USS Mathews and USS Belle Grove reached Okinawa on February 4, bringing the remaining attached units aboard those ships.

At sea, preparation continued through formal instruction and physical training. The Marines studied general military subjects, Vietnam orientation and landmine warfare. On reaching Okinawa, their training shifted to field work and live firing.
After debarkation, the landing team’s attachments returned to their parent organizations. The battalion came under the 1st Marine Division on February 2, then the 5th Marines on February 5.

precision: The curved arrow shows the journey from Pearl Harbor toward Camp Schwab, not a verified ship track or landing berth. Arrival dates refer to Okinawa, not a documented arrival time at Camp Schwab. Calendar-date spans are not exact elapsed sailing times across the International Date Line.
